entries.reason: Renamed Rust crates still contain ADR-020-governed PQUEUE_* configuration aliases, persisted pqueue_* identifiers, RESP pqueue tokens, and historical bead references; the dedicated namespace checks reject old packages/imports while permitting only declared [[bin]] compatibility aliases and requiring Fireweed-primary process environment reads.
entries.owner_surface: Rust runtime compatibility, persistence/wire identifiers, and audit references
entries.removal_condition: Remove after v0.20.0 consumers migrate from the declared binary and PQUEUE_* aliases and the configuration, protocol, persisted-data, and audit owners retire the remaining governed identifiers.

entries.reason: The Fireweed chart still renders ADR-020-governed runtime environment aliases and retained on-disk identifiers, and names historical bead IDs for auditability. The verifier evaluates identity tokens without surrounding path context, so this rule admits chart-local pqueue tokens while the dedicated deployment-coordinate layer independently rejects old chart, workload, image, label, package, and evidence coordinates.
entries.owner_surface: Helm runtime configuration, persisted paths, and audit references
entries.removal_condition: Remove after the configuration and persisted-data owners retire the remaining PQUEUE runtime aliases and pqueue storage identifiers.

entries.reason: The live Postgres and S3 test harnesses still read these v0.20.0 compatibility variables and the historical MinIO fixture bucket; checkout paths, Cargo coordinates, binaries, release variables, and public workflow labels have moved to Fireweed.
entries.owner_surface: GitHub Actions provisioned integration-test compatibility inputs
entries.removal_condition: Remove when every provisioned integration-test harness reads FIREWEED_* as its primary input and the retained MinIO fixture bucket is migrated.

entries.reason: ADR-020 distinguishes operator-facing examples from retained on-disk and runtime wire identifiers such as /var/lib/pqueue and PQUEUE_* compatibility variables.
entries.removal_condition: Remove after public deployment examples use Fireweed coordinates and any retained pqueue storage or wire identifiers are covered by a separate data-migration ADR.

entries.reason: ADR-020 preserves historical release notes, evidence ledgers, benchmark commands, and audit artifacts without rewriting published history.
entries.owner_surface: Release evidence, performance evidence, and historical release notes
entries.removal_condition: Remove only if a later evidence-retention decision supersedes the no-history-rewrite policy for these tracked artifacts.

entries.reason: ADR-020 keeps historical naming analysis, bead IDs, accepted decisions, and migration inventory visible for auditability.
